title: Describe, approve, build, accept: four things you do; PL does the rest
prompt: How can I use this platform to build a software application?
summary: You describe the problem and answer a few questions, approve the Blueprint and the work products, send Start build, and accept the release. PL discovers, designs, generates, verifies and releases.
takeaways: Four things you do: describe, approve, start the build, accept the release.
About 30 to 45 minutes of your attention for a simple application.
You never write code, design tables or configure servers.

blocks.caption: Your part is the bold verbs. PL never moves past an approval on its own.

rows.label: Input
rows.value: A few sentences: who struggles, how work happens now, what should improve, the fields and rules that matter.

rows.label: Output
rows.value: A running application with UI, API, PostgreSQL schema, roles, tests, evidence and a release you can open in EAL.

rows.label: Your time
rows.value: Typically 30 to 45 minutes of attention for a simple application; PL works in the background between your approvals.

rows.label: What you never do
rows.value: Write code, design tables, configure servers, or copy files. Those are generated, verified and recorded.

blocks.title: Mileage Reimbursement Log
blocks.before: Employees email trip details; finance recalculates amounts by hand; nobody knows which claims are approved.
blocks.after: Employees log trips with miles and rate; the app computes the reimbursement with the agreed rounding rule; managers approve from a worklist; finance sees only approved claims.

title: From words to a working app: understanding, blueprint, generation
prompt: How does the platform take an idea or business requirement and turn it into a working application?
summary: A model-driven understanding turns your words into typed discovery items; the Blueprint fixes entity, fields, states, roles and screens; deterministic generators compile it into code; delivery provisions, builds, verifies and registers it.

blocks.caption: Intelligence is used to understand and shape; generation is deterministic so it can be verified.

rows.label: Understanding
rows.value: The understanding engine extracts a domain-neutral outcome from the conversation: goal, users, current state, desired change.

rows.label: Discovery
rows.value: Outcome discovery produces items with lifecycle and authority: proposed, tentatively accepted, accepted, disputed. Semantic defects (for example an unsupported confirmation) block readiness until resolved.

rows.label: Blueprint
rows.value: When enough dimensions are covered, the Discovery Blueprint is generated for your approval. It is the canonical input for everything downstream.

rows.label: Application blueprint
rows.value: From approved requirements, one structured call derives the entity, fields, states, roles and floorplan bindings as typed data.

rows.label: Generation
rows.value: Schema-driven generators and the floorplan compiler emit domain types, migration, API routes with role policy and idempotency, and the React UI. No model writes code.

rows.label: Delivery
rows.value: Provision schema and login, migrate, build, start on reserved ports, verify with tests and a browser, register with EAL, publish roles to UME.

blocks.text: Because generation is deterministic, the same Blueprint always produces the same files, and every file carries a SHA-256 in the artifact manifest. That is what makes the result reviewable.

title: Six stages from discovery to production, with the gate at each
prompt: What are the major stages involved in developing an application from discovery through production?
summary: Discovery, shaping, design and planning, build and verification, release and run, operate and improve. Each stage ends in a typed gate you control. Production promotion beyond Local Development is planned, not yet available.

items.label: 1 Discovery
items.detail: Gate: Discovery Blueprint approved

items.label: 2 Shaping
items.detail: Gate: landscape confirmed; Requirements approved

items.label: 3 Design and planning
items.detail: Gate: Delivery Plan, Solution Design, Build Plan approved

items.label: 4 Build and verification
items.detail: Gate: tests and browser qualification pass; Start build authorized by you

items.label: 5 Release and run
items.detail: Gate: Business Review accepted; release activated in EAL

items.label: 6 Operate and improve
items.detail: Gate per change: impact approved; new version verified

blocks.caption: Gates are typed events in the delivery case, never inferred from chat.

rows: Planned: release manifests promoted through environment gates

title: The complete delivery process, end to end
prompt: Walk me through the complete end-to-end application delivery process using this platform.
summary: Twelve concrete steps from project creation to a user signing in, with the command or click at each step and the evidence produced.

blocks.caption: Then: Business Review, release activation, open in EAL, first record.

items.title: 1 Create a project
items.detail: Projects panel: Create. One application per project; the project holds the primary chat and its successors.

items.title: 2 Describe and discover
items.detail: Send the problem description ending with Finalize discovery from this description and generate the Discovery Blueprint for review. Do not design or build yet. Accept the 2 to 5 measurable defaults PL proposes.

items.title: 3 Approve the Discovery Blueprint
items.detail: Read entity, fields, states, roles, floorplans and the topology recommendation. Approve, or request a change and approve the next version.

items.title: 4 Confirm the landscape
items.detail: Click Use Local defaults and confirm. PL composes, resolves and confirms UI port, API port and PostgreSQL schema.

items.title: 5 Requirements
items.detail: Send the next-step command: Create the Requirements for the current app from the approved Discovery Blueprint. Show it for review. Do not build or create files yet. Approve.

items.title: 6 Delivery Plan and Solution Design
items.detail: Same pattern, in order. The Solution Design shows components and data ownership; approve.

items.title: 7 Build Plan
items.detail: Exact files, migrations and tests. Approve. Now all four heads are on the active revision.

items.title: 8 Start build.
items.detail: PL scaffolds, generates, provisions the schema and login, migrates, builds, starts on reserved ports, runs typecheck, tests and browser qualification, and records the release identity.

items.title: 9 Business Review
items.detail: A table of checks with browser evidence. Accept the release, or reject with a reason.

items.title: 10 Activation
items.detail: The signed release set is staged and activated in the EAL registry; roles are published to UME; a test identity pl.app-name.user is created.

items.title: 11 Open in EAL
items.detail: Click Open in EAL, sign in with the test identity, create the first record through the registered form.

items.title: 12 Evolve
items.detail: Describe a change in the same project; PL shows the impact, regenerates in order, verifies and releases version 1.0.1.

items.label: Landscape

items.label: Work products

items.label: Release

title: Decisions and approvals across the lifecycle
prompt: What decisions and approvals would typically occur throughout the delivery lifecycle?
summary: Clarification answers and default acceptances during discovery; Blueprint approval; landscape confirmation; four work-product approvals with a cascade; Start build authorization; Business Review acceptance; per-change impact approval; effect grants for anything external.

rows: Answer a clarification or accept a measurable default
A discovery item becomes accepted with your authority
Opens the requirements stage; the Blueprint becomes canonical
Fixes where the app will run
Starts the chain; a later change supersedes the three downstream products
Approve Delivery Plan, Solution Design, Build Plan
Starts a bounded evolution and a new version
Required for anything outside the workspace; none in Local Development apps

blocks.title: The cascade
blocks.text: Approving a new Requirements or Delivery Plan version supersedes its dependents. Regenerate in order: Requirements, Delivery Plan, Solution Design, Build Plan. Request change text is stored as a rejection; fix content in Requirements rather than at Build Plan review.

title: The complete application lifecycle as a process flow
prompt: Show me the complete lifecycle of an application built using this platform as a process flow.
summary: A single flow from problem to version n, with the loop back from operations to the next revision.

blocks.caption: Every later version. Unrelated behaviour is preserved and proven by the existing tests.

rows.label: Loop owner
rows.value: PL owns the development thread; EAL owns runtime task cases; UME owns identity; the application owns its data.

rows.label: Version identity
rows.value: Each release has an identity and a manifest; superseded releases stay immutable on disk and can be rolled back.

rows.label: Retire
rows.value: Revoke the release in EAL; the schema and evidence remain until an explicit retention decision.
